the user wants to understand how a syste.rule: The user wants to understand how a system works through explanation (what it does, when each piece runs, how data looks in tables) before deploying or changing it
the user wants to understand how a syste.instead: Explain mechanics concretely: what runs when, what each component does, and show example data/records from their own test inputs. Answer the exact question asked.
the user wants to understand how a syste.why: They asked what the app does, how notes look in the Dynamo tables, when Haiku classifies and when topics get created, and the category vs topic difference.

the user communicates in both english an.rule: The user communicates in both English and Spanish (casual, typo-prone, lowercase) and expects replies in the language they last used
the user communicates in both english an.instead: Reply in Spanish (rioplatense, informal voseo) when the user writes in Spanish; otherwise English. Tolerate typos and interpret intent.
the user communicates in both english an.why: They switched to Spanish for the design discussion ('ayudame a entender...', 'explicame como funcionaria...') and Claude answered in Spanish; earlier messages were in English with typos.

the user wants design discussion and tra.rule: The user wants design discussion and trade-off recommendations before implementation, with worked examples using their own scenario
the user wants design discussion and tra.instead: For design questions, recommend a schema/approach with trade-offs, then walk through a concrete multi-step example (e.g. week by week) using their examples; ask before moving to formal design or coding.
the user wants design discussion and tra.why: They asked which design best fits their evolving-hierarchy idea, then asked for an incremental walk-through over 3 weeks.

the user uses uv to run python in this p.rule: The user uses uv to run Python in this project
the user uses uv to run python in this p.instead: Use `uv run ...` for running scripts and tests.
the user uses uv to run python in this p.why: Project commands like `uv run python dev.py` and `uv run pytest` were used and accepted.

the user writes in spanish rioplatense w.rule: The user writes in Spanish (Rioplatense) with short, informal messages and expects replies in Spanish
the user writes in spanish rioplatense w.instead: Reply in Spanish, in a conversational register. Keep code, identifiers and commit messages in English as the repo does.
the user writes in spanish rioplatense w.why: Every user message is in short, informal Spanish and Claude's replies in Spanish were accepted without complaint.

the user explores a behaviour one scenar.rule: The user explores a behaviour one scenario at a time and wants to see each result before moving on
the user explores a behaviour one scenar.instead: Build and run one test scenario per step (reparent, then merge, then rename) and report the result briefly. Then ask which scenario comes next.
the user explores a behaviour one scenar.why: They stepped through the reparent, merge and rename cases with 'ahora merge', 'ahora el rename', and asked for a separate script for each.

the user is comfortable letting claude r.rule: The user is comfortable letting Claude run deploy and AWS commands (terraform apply or destroy, lambda update, invoke) after a brief confirmation
the user is comfortable letting claude r.instead: For infrastructure work, state what will happen (e.g. the number of resources destroyed), get a quick OK, then run it and verify the result. Hand over only interactive steps like auth login.
the user is comfortable letting claude r.why: They answered 'Correlo yo' for terraform destroy, and replied 'dale' and 'si' to Claude redeploying and invoking the Lambda.

the user wants a diagnosis first without.rule: The user wants a diagnosis first, without changes being made yet
the user wants a diagnosis first without.instead: When the user asks to diagnose a problem, investigate and report the cause and a proposed fix, and leave code, infra and deploys unchanged until they say to apply it. Ask before making the change.
the user wants a diagnosis first without.why: They asked to "make a diagnose" of slow app opening on their phone and did not ask for a fix.

the user wants claude to report warnings.rule: The user wants Claude to report warnings and errors from tool runs in its answer, not silently dismiss them
the user wants claude to report warnings.instead: If a run prints stderr warnings or errors, mention them briefly in the result, say whether they matter, and suggest a fix.
the user wants claude to report warnings.why: After a summary that omitted the NumPy warning, the user asked "did you have an error?".
